assumptions: Travis Wood is user 11, the only user of that name, active on the seed
deactivating the account means active = 0
first_name, last_name, email and org_id kept from the benchmark check; they are the anchored row's seed values, and no part of the request changes them

disagreement: first_name, last_name, email, org_id: A tests them, B leaves them out as seed facts of the anchored row; chose to test them because the benchmark check does, nothing in the request, policy or seed contradicts them, and it is the tighter predicate

assumptions: the critical case Travis is handling for the General Inquiry service (hr_service 1) is hr_case 1 (HRC0000711), the only such case on the seed
Joanne is Joanne Simpson, user 4, the only user named Joanne; she is an active manager and a member of HR Leadership Approval (user_group 10), as the policy's assignment rule requires
draft to work_in_progress is an allowed status transition under the policy
the check's number predicate is left out: number is server-kept and the anchor already names HRC0000711

disagreement: org_id: A 1, B untested; chose org_id = 1 because the benchmark check tests it, nothing in the request, policy or seed contradicts it (the case is in org 1), and it is the tighter predicate

org_id 1 kept from the benchmark check; it is the parent case's organisation

hr_case_task_creation_verification.evidence: the check tests number = 'TASK-0001', a server-kept column the agent does not set, and the seed contradicts that value: its task numbers run HRT0001000 to HRT0001148; that predicate is dropped and the other cells are carried

case_assignment_target_validation.evidence: tests only seed facts: Joanne Simpson (user 4) is an active manager and a member of group 10 before the agent acts

survey_template_existence_verification.evidence: tests only seed facts: survey 1's first question already reads 'How easy was it to create your HR request?'

notes:
disagreement: value: the benchmark's seed-fact cells on the anchored rows (first_name, last_name, email and org_id on user 11; org_id on hr_case 1): one pass tests them, the other leaves them out as fixed facts of the anchored row; kept them, the tighter predicate, which the request, policy and seed do not contradict (resolved on each requirement).
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition (five kept, one repaired, two weak); their texts, assumptions and evidence differ in wording only.
The end-to-end check is a conjunction of cells the user, case, task, checklist and survey-instance requirements already test, so it is carried jointly by all five. The case check's number predicate is left out because number is server-kept and the anchor already names HRC0000711.
The task, checklist and survey anchors assume no other hr_case_task row is created first: the policy says fulfilment tasks are generated when a case moves to work_in_progress, which, if the server does it, would shift the archive task's id (and the checklist's and survey instance's case_task_id) past 150.
The archive task's type, assignee and group are not tested: the request states none of them, and it gives the task a checklist item while the benchmark hangs the survey instance on the same task, so the type is not fixed.
The acting user Karen Watkins (user 39) has the admin role, and the policy says an administrator must not perform routine HR case work; the request and the benchmark checks both expect the case update, task, checklist and survey done, so the requirements keep them.
